meta.title: Rewards World™ | Pay you can cost, explain and defend

hero.title: Pay you can cost, explain and defend.
hero.lead: A plan can look fine in the deck. Then it shows up in the accounts as a number nobody worked out. We design the pay plan, cost it, and defend it with the people who build it and the people who have to sign it. A working tool sits behind every piece of work.

questions: What behaviour it is meant to buy.
What it still pays after the meeting.
What breaks in a bad year.

hero.tagline: Design it. Cost it. Govern it.

who.title: For the people who build the number, and the people who sign it.
who.lead: Here is how each seat usually puts it, and what we put in front of them. The practice is rooted in India. The clients may be here or around the world.

people.says: I want to pay people fairly and hire well, without my pay bill running ahead of me. I do not have an HR team to build this.
people.gives: Clean levels and Fixed CTC bands, with the cost of every move on one page.

people.says: I have to explain every pay decision to employees, to the CEO and to the committee. I cannot do that from ten spreadsheets.
people.gives: One place for the data, plain explanations on every screen, and approvals on record.

people.says: Tell me what it costs this year, what it costs later and what happens in a bad year, in numbers that tie to the accounts.
people.gives: The cash, the profit and loss and the accounting charge on one page.

people.says: I have to sign this. I want to see what was rejected, not only what is recommended, and who approved it.
people.gives: A short paper the committee can decide on, with sources, assumptions and risks.

who.entitiesNote: The tool is built around Indian law and Indian legal forms, from a start-up to a listed company, and for an LLP, a bank or an insurer. It asks for your legal form and your regulator, then shows the checks that apply to you. We do this work for organisations in India and for clients around the world. Anything not yet checked by a legal adviser is marked draft.

samples.title: Three outputs from the work
samples.lead: Each piece of work ends in a page you can take into a meeting. Your data, its source and the name of who approved it sit on the page.
items: A short board page that answers four questions in one place: what it costs this year, what it is meant to achieve, what it costs later, and what breaks in a bad year. Sources, assumptions and risks sit on the same page, with a version stamp and the name of who approved it.
A set of Fixed CTC bands by grade, with placement rules and a one-page view of where each person lands and what it costs to move them in.

A list of the Indian checks that apply to your legal form and your regulator, each with its source and date. Each line shows what needs attention, for review by your legal adviser. It is not a legal opinion.
